# Bubba's Infused Gems: balance model

Generated by `tools/gem-balance.py` from the owner's design in `specs/effect-gems.md`. Do not edit by hand: change the script and rerun it. Vanilla numbers come from the decompiled Minecraft 26.3 source and the script re-checks them against it.

## The formula in plain words

- **A gem doesn't care where it goes** (owner). Every gem, from any potion, item or loot, fits armor (3 slots a piece) or a weapon (2 slots). **The slot decides who its effects reach:** in armor, the wearer; in a weapon, what it hits (bows and crossbows: the arrow). All of a gem's effects go the same way: main effect, any other effect and any drawback. So a Poison gem in your armor poisons you, and a Regeneration gem on a sword heals the target: allowed, just pointless.
- **There is one Infused Gem item** (owner); the base gem it was brewed from is its **Infusion level**: Infusion I (amethyst), Infusion II (quartz), Infusion III (ender pearl), Infusion IV (diamond), Infusion V (prismarine shard), Infusion VI (nether star). Names read like *Infused Gem: Infusion III, Speed (Splash)*.
- Every effect has **two curves on one scale**, 1.0 = the strongest vanilla level. **Worn** (armor): the effect on the wearer all the time, 1.0 = the strongest level of the effect (Speed II, Strength II, Resistance IV...), on/off effects made partial. **Hit-applied** (weapon): what one hit gives the target, 1.0 = the strongest vanilla potion of that effect as drunk (owner: potions, not tipped arrows), so a hit is a nerfed potion. Healing has its own, flatter worn curve.
- **One gem's strength** = potion factor x Infusion factor x enchant grade x gear factor. In armor the gear factor is armor material x matching run; in a weapon it is the weapon's material. Each is at most 1.0.
- **Armor stacking:** a piece holds 3 gems, so 12 in all. The gems of one effect are lined up strongest first; the first counts fully, each next one 85% of the one before. The sum is scaled so that 12 perfect gems give exactly **0.9**.
- **Weapon stacking:** a weapon holds 2 gems, same rule, scaled so 2 perfect gems give exactly **0.9**. One perfect gem gives 0.486: two gems of one effect, or one gem each of two effects.
- **The cap is 0.9**: 5% short of vanilla's best. Only the single best build reaches it: **lingering potion + Infusion VI (nether star) + tier 3 + full contiguous netherite** (armor), or **+ a netherite weapon with both slots** (weapons).
- **Potion form doesn't multiply**: it sets the highest enchant tier (normal 1, splash 2, lingering 3), and the tier sets the grade. So lingering is needed for the strongest grade.
- **Infusion level changes strength only** (owner): no traits. Order, by how hard the base gem is to get: amethyst, quartz, ender pearl, diamond, prismarine shard, nether star.
- **One roll table per gem** (owner): its main effect, maybe an **other** effect of the same kind (a beneficial gem's bonus is another beneficial effect, a harmful gem's another harmful one, never the main effect itself), maybe a **drawback** of the opposite kind that is **never the main effect's direct opposite**. The other effect uses the same formula with its own grade and joins that effect's stack; a drawback is a fixed, mild size (below).

Total for an effect, in symbols: `total = 0.9 x sum(gem_i x 0.85^(rank_i)) / sum(0.85^0..0.85^(slots-1))`, with `gem = potion x infusion x grade x gear`.

### Potion form -> highest enchant tier (owner)

| Form | Highest tier | Best grade reachable |
|---|---|---|
| Normal | 1 | weak |
| Splash | 2 | medium |
| Lingering | 3 | strongest |

The form is the potion's form, fixed at brewing; nothing raises it later (owner: potion -> gem, no other pathway). An Infused Gem brewed from an item has no potion form: it reaches tier 3, like a lingering potion's gem (owner, 2026-11-15: every gem should be able to reach the cap unless it proves too strong; collecting twelve of the item is the cost). `ITEM_MAX_TIER_OVERRIDE` can cap one source later.

### Weapon material (proposal: a factor, like armor)

Yes for consistency: the same gem is stronger in a better weapon, exactly as in better armor, so a netherite weapon is part of the single best build. Swords, axes and spears come in every material. Bows, crossbows, tridents and maces have none, so they get a fixed diamond-level factor: they can't be upgraded, and at diamond-level the best build stays unique to netherite.

## Every status effect: craftable, found-only, or not a gem

Every one of the 40 status effects in 26.3 (the script reads them from the source and fails if one is missing). Any gem goes into armor or a weapon. An effect with a potion is brewed from it. One without a potion is brewed from a vanilla item that already carries it: in 26.3 the brewing stand's bottle slot takes any item that a brewing recipe names as its input (BrewingStandMenu.PotionSlot asks the recipes, PotionIngredient.isPotionInput), so this is data, no menu change. Stews are told apart by their stew effect with Fabric API's components ingredient. An effect with no sensible item is a **found-only** gem: loot and mob gear, never brewed.

### Found-only gems: what they come with

A found gem is made as if brewed and enchanted: its potion factor is 1.0 (one form of the effect), its Infusion level is picked from the loot source's list and its tier rolled from the source's tiers with the normal tier odds. Same strength scale as crafted gems; only ominous loot can give a perfect one.

| Loot source | Infusion levels | Tiers | Strength range (gem quality) |

| Common loot (dungeons, mineshafts, temples, shipwrecks, ruins, fishing treasure, hero gifts, most mobs) | Infusion I (amethyst), Infusion I (amethyst), Infusion II (quartz) | 1 | 0.20 - 0.25 (or a drawback-only roll at tier 1) |
| Rare loot (strongholds, buried treasure, outposts, mansions, nether fortresses, piglins) | Infusion I (amethyst), Infusion II (quartz), Infusion II (quartz), Infusion III (ender pearl) | 1, 1, 2 | 0.20 - 0.46 (or a drawback-only roll at tier 1) |
| Hard places (ancient cities, bastions, end cities, trial vaults, elder guardians, trial chamber mobs) | Infusion II (quartz), Infusion III (ender pearl), Infusion III (ender pearl), Infusion IV (diamond) | 1, 2, 2 | 0.25 - 0.56 (or a drawback-only roll at tier 1) |
| Ominous vaults in trial chambers | Infusion III (ender pearl), Infusion IV (diamond), Infusion IV (diamond), Infusion V (prismarine shard), Infusion VI (nether star) | 2, 2, 3 | 0.46 - 1.00 |

## Loot: where gems are found (one table, `LOOT_PLACES`)

Every place below gets **one extra roll** with the given chance per chest (fishing: per treasure catch; hero gift: per gift; elder guardian: per kill by a player). The roll adds a finished gem of any craftable effect, or a gemmed armor piece of the level's materials (20%), or a gemmed weapon (15%), or, where found-only gems are listed, one of them (a third of the time). Vanilla's tables are never replaced; the extra roll is a data file of the mod (`loot_table/inject/...`), so a datapack can change or empty any of it. Rare and mostly weak, better in harder places (owner). Only ominous vaults use Infusion VI, and there it is always a perfect gem (tier 3, full strength) of any effect, which comes with a drawback except 5% of the time (owner); elsewhere loot never gives a craftable gem Infusion VI.

### Gems on mobs

Each armor piece and weapon a mob spawns with gets gems with the chance below; the mob gets the gems' effects like a player (undead follow the undead rules). The piece drops with vanilla's equipment drop chance and keeps its gems. Mobs from ominous trial spawners wear vanilla's trial equipment table, which gets gems too; they never drop their gear (vanilla).

| Who | Level | Chance per armor piece or weapon | Gems |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mobs spawning in ancient cities, bastions, end cities, woodland mansions, ocean monuments, nether fortresses and pillager outposts | hard | 7% | 1-2 |
| Raid mobs (pillagers, vindicators... in a raid) | hard | 7% | 1-2 |
| Raid captains (the same rate) | hard | 7% | 1-2 |
| Piglins elsewhere | rare | 1.5% | 1 |
| Every other mob that spawns with armor or a weapon (zombies, husks, drowned with tridents, skeletons and strays with bows...) | common | 1% | 1 |
| Ominous trial spawner mobs | hard | 10% | 1-2 |

Weapons (and gemmed weapons in chests) roll their gems from the harmful effects 75% of the time and from any gem otherwise (owner: they hit the player).

## Roll tables

One roll table per gem, whatever slot it later goes into. **Other** (tier 2 weak, tier 3 weak or medium): any gem effect of the main effect's kind except itself and the main-effect-only ones (Healing: its own per-hit curve: main effect only; Harming: a strike on every hit: main effect only; Hero of the Village: a permanent villager discount stays a rare found gem: main effect only). **Drawback** (tier 1 alone, tier 3 with the strongest main effect): one of the opposite kind, never the main effect's direct opposite.

### Direct opposites (never a drawback of each other)

| Beneficial | Harmful | Why they cancel out |
|---|---|---|
| Speed | Slowness | movement speed up / down (owner) |
| Strength | Weakness | attack damage up / down (owner) |
| Haste | Mining Fatigue | mining and attack speed up / down (owner) |
| Regeneration | Poison | health over time back / away (owner) |
| Regeneration | Wither | health over time back / away (owner) |
| Luck | Bad Luck | luck +1 / -1 (owner) |
| Healing | Harming | instant heal / instant damage (owner) |
| Saturation | Hunger | food kept / food drained (owner) |
| Night Vision | Blindness | sight in the dark / no sight (owner) |
| Night Vision | Darkness | sight in the dark / pulsing dark (owner) |
| Invisibility | Glowing | hidden / outlined through walls (owner) |
| Slow Falling | Levitation | slower fall / forced rise (owner) |
| Conduit Power | Mining Fatigue | added: Conduit Power's underwater mining is the conduit's Haste, and Mining Fatigue is the ocean monument's direct answer to it |

Checked and left out (no direct opposite in vanilla): **Jump Boost**: no vanilla effect lowers jumps; Slow Falling / Levitation is a different axis (falling, not jumping); **Resistance**: no vanilla effect raises damage taken; Weakness lowers damage dealt, which is Strength's opposite; **Health Boost**: no vanilla effect lowers max health; Wither drains health over time, which is Regeneration's opposite; **Absorption**: no vanilla effect takes absorption away; same reasoning as Health Boost; **Fire Resistance**: no vanilla effect makes fire hurt more; **Water Breathing**: no vanilla effect drains air faster; **Dolphin's Grace**: no vanilla effect slows swimming alone; Slowness is Speed's opposite; **Hero of the Village**: its opposite is Bad Omen, which is not a gem or a drawback. Harmful effects with no beneficial counterpart: Nausea, Wind Charged, Weaving, Oozing, Infested.

### Drawback candidates

A beneficial gem's drawback rolls from: Slowness, Weakness, Mining Fatigue, Hunger, Bad Luck, Poison, Wither. A harmful gem's drawback rolls from: Speed, Strength, Jump Boost, Regeneration, Resistance, Turtle Master, Fire Resistance, Water Breathing, Night Vision, Invisibility, Slow Falling, Luck, Silence, Breeze, Haste, Absorption, Health Boost, Dolphin's Grace, Saturation, Conduit Power, Hero of the Village. Minus the main effect's direct opposite, which leaves every gem at least 5 candidates. Never a drawback: Harming (instant, no mild form); Healing (instant, no mild form); Blindness (ruins the screen, not just the gem); Darkness (ruins the screen, not just the gem); Nausea (ruins the screen, not just the gem); Levitation (dangerous, not mild); Glowing (harmless alone, a beacon in PvP); Wind Burst (an action, no mild level); Weaving (an action, no mild level); Oozing (an action, no mild level); Infested (spawns mobs, not mild).

## In armor: what each gem does to the wearer

Beneficial gems are what armor is for. Harmful gems in armor hit the wearer (pointless, but allowed): damage-over-time and attribute effects at the same level as their hit anchor, Glowing on all the time, Darkness, Blindness and Nausea as a steady, partial dimming, fog or wobble on the wearer's screen, Levitation a slow drift up by strength (owner), death and hurt triggers as a chance. Harming in armor mirrors the Healing gem: each survivable hit taken deals a share more.

## Healing gem (in armor)

When the wearer takes damage from an attack or a fall and survives it, they instantly get back a fraction of the health that hit took. A killing blow still kills. Its own curve: `heal = 0.25 x (total / 0.9)^0.7`, so the best build returns exactly 25% and early gems are flattened upward to stay noticeable. On a weapon it heals the target a little on every hit (below).

**Why 25% at the very best:** it works like 25% less damage from survivable hits, between Resistance I (20%) and Resistance II (40%), and far below the Resistance gem's own best (76%) or full Protection IV armor (64%). It never stops a one-shot, never heals outside a fight, and is always a net loss (you can't farm it with fall damage). A Healing II potion gives 8 HP at once; at 25% the wearer must take 32 HP of hits, about one and a half health bars, to get that much back. So it is a comfort in long fights, not a second health bar.

| Build | Gem total | Share of each hit returned | A 6 HP zombie hit | A 20 HP fall (survived) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Starter | 0.018 | 1.6% | +0.10 HP | +0.3 HP |
| Early | 0.097 | 5.3% | +0.32 HP | +1.1 HP |
| Mid | 0.367 | 13.3% | +0.80 HP | +2.7 HP |
| Late | 0.698 | 20.9% | +1.25 HP | +4.2 HP |
| Best | 1.000 | 26.9% | +1.61 HP | +5.4 HP |

## In a weapon: what one hit gives the target

A weapon holds 2 gems. Swords, axes, maces, tridents and spears apply the gem's effects to what they hit; bows and crossbows turn each fired arrow into its tipped form carrying them (picked up again, it's a plain arrow). Each hit **refreshes** the effect, it never stacks. A real tipped arrow fired from a gemmed bow: the stronger effect applies (higher strength wins, then longer duration), never both. Harmful gems are what weapons are for; a beneficial gem on a weapon buffs the target (pointless, but allowed).

**Per hit (owner):** potency is measured against the strongest potion level: potency = s^0.5 of the 1.0 level (it approaches Poison II, Slowness IV... at the cap, never reaching it). Duration is short: at most 8 s from the best weapon build, x (s / cap)^0.5 below it, and never under the effect's floor, so every hit does something a player notices: Darkness 3 s, Regeneration long enough to heal 2 HP, everything else 2 s. Each hit refreshes, it never adds. On/off harmful effects (Wind Charged, Weaving, Oozing, Infested, Glowing, Levitation, Blindness, Nausea, Darkness) are the vanilla effect, their strength all in duration. Harming and Healing strike on every hit (owner): s x 2.5 magic damage or s x 2 HP healed on the target, at least 1, a modest bonus below Sharpness V's +3.

## Drawbacks

A drawback roll is a fixed size: **10% of the strongest vanilla level** of that effect for a weak one, 15% for tier 3's medium one, whatever the potion, Infusion level or gear (a better gem shouldn't hurt more). More drawbacks of the same effect add less and less and never pass 20%, which is below vanilla's weakest level of every drawback effect. So they sting, but never as much as a real potion of it. It goes where the gem's main effect goes: in armor, on the wearer while worn; in a weapon, on the target for 3 s, refreshed by each hit (a beneficial gem's harmful drawback on a weapon therefore lands on the target too).

### How each effect is made partial

| Effect | Implementation | Source (26.3) |
|---|---|---|
| Speed | Attribute modifier on movement_speed, +0.4 x s, add_multiplied_total (exact). | MobEffects.SPEED |
| Strength | Attribute modifier on attack_damage, +6 x s, add_value (exact). | MobEffects.STRENGTH |
| Jump Boost | Attribute modifiers: jump_strength +0.2 x s and safe_fall_distance +2 x s. (Vanilla adds the jump boost after the block jump factor; the attribute is scaled by it, so it is a little weaker on honey.) | MobEffects.JUMP_BOOST, LivingEntity.getJumpBoostPower, Attributes.JUMP_STRENGTH 0.42 |
| Regeneration | Tick handler: heal 0.8 x s / 20 HP per tick while hurt (LivingEntity.heal takes floats). Not a MobEffectInstance, because vanilla levels are whole numbers. | RegenerationMobEffect |
| Resistance | Damage hook (mixin at LivingEntity.getDamageAfterMagicAbsorb, beside vanilla's resistance), x (1 - 0.4 x s), skipping bypasses_resistance damage. With Turtle Master gems or a vanilla Resistance effect, the strongest reduction applies. | LivingEntity.getDamageAfterMagicAbsorb, BeaconBlockEntity |
| Turtle Master | Both parts at strength s: the resistance damage hook x (1 - 0.8 x s) and a movement_speed modifier -0.9 x s (add_multiplied_total). Against Resistance gems the strongest reduction applies. | Potions.STRONG_TURTLE_MASTER (Slowness 400 ticks amplifier 5, Resistance amplifier 3) |
| Fire Resistance | On/off made partial: fire-tagged damage (is_fire) x (1 - s) through the damage hook, and burning_time attribute -s (add_multiplied_total) so fire also goes out sooner. | LivingEntity (is_fire + FIRE_RESISTANCE), Entity lava 4.0, Attributes.BURNING_TIME |
| Water Breathing | On/off made partial with the vanilla oxygen_bonus attribute (what Respiration uses): bonus = s / (1 - s), so each air tick is kept with chance s. Pure attribute, exact. | LivingEntity.decreaseAirSupply, Entity.getMaxAirSupply 300 |
| Night Vision | On/off made partial on the client: set the lightmap's nightVisionEffectIntensity to s (mixin at LightmapRenderStateExtractor, where vanilla writes GameRenderer.nightVisionScale). Vanilla already renders fractional values during its end-fade. | GameRenderer.nightVisionScale, LightmapRenderStateExtractor |
| Invisibility | Stealth that scales (owner, Q33): mobs' visibility check x (1 - 0.93 x s) (hook at LivingEntity.getVisibilityPercent), hidden on the locator bar from s 0.5 (waypoint_transmit_range -100%), and only the perfect complete set (s = the cap) gives the real vanilla effect, see-through body and all; armor renders as in vanilla. | LivingEntity.getVisibilityPercent, item/component/MobVisibility, MobEffects.INVISIBILITY |
| Slow Falling | On/off made partial: while falling, gravity 0.08 - 0.07 x s up to the potion's 0.01 at s = 1, past it 0.01 / s (mixin at LivingEntity.getEffectiveGravity, where vanilla checks slow falling) and fall_damage_multiplier -s. | LivingEntity.getEffectiveGravity, Attributes.GRAVITY 0.08 |
| Luck | Attribute modifier on luck, +s (exact). | MobEffects.LUCK |
| Healing | After the wearer takes damage from an attack (an entity source) or a fall and survives it, heal that damage instance's health loss x the gem's fraction, at once. A killing blow still kills (the heal runs after the hit, only if the wearer is alive). Mixin after LivingEntity.actuallyHurt. Works the same on mobs. | LivingEntity.actuallyHurt, DamageTypeTags.IS_FALL, HealOrHarmMobEffect |
| Poison | Gem Poison mob effect (vanilla's icon and rules; potency in 1% steps): never below 1 HP, undead immune, milk clears it. | PoisonMobEffect, Potions.STRONG_POISON |
| Slowness | Gem Slowness mob effect: movement_speed -0.6 x potency (add_multiplied_total). As a drawback: the same modifier, permanent while worn. | MobEffects.SLOWNESS, Potions.STRONG_SLOWNESS |
| Weakness | Gem Weakness mob effect: attack_damage -4 x potency. As a drawback: the same modifier, permanent while worn. | MobEffects.WEAKNESS, Potions.LONG_WEAKNESS |
| Harming | On a weapon: every hit or arrow deals +2.5 x s magic damage (at least 1.0). Undead are healed instead, as in vanilla. In armor: the Healing gem's mirror. | HealOrHarmMobEffect |
| Wind Burst | Worn: when the wearer would take fall damage, it is x (1 - s/cap) and a small wind burst (sound and particles) bounces them up at WIND_LAND_BOUNCE_BEST x s/cap. Hit: the target is thrown up (WIND_HIT_UP_BEST x s/cap) and away from the attacker (WIND_HIT_PUSH_BEST x s/cap); on a mace with the Wind Burst enchantment, x WIND_MACE_BONUS past the cap (owner). | WindChargedMobEffect, AbstractWindCharge, MaceItem |
| Weaving | Worn: the cobweb slowdown (Entity.makeStuckInBlock) moves s/cap of the way to none. Hit: a chance (WEAVING_WEB_CHANCE_BEST x s/cap) to place a real cobweb at the target's feet, only into air, never replacing a block; it stays (owner). | WebBlock, WeavingMobEffect |
| Oozing | Worn: fall damage x (1 - s/cap) and the wearer bounced back up with OOZING_BOUNCE_BEST x s/cap of the impact speed. Hit: a kill splits off 1-2 small slimes, neutral (no attack goals), owned by the attacker (isAlliedTo, stored on the slime), never despawning while loaded but never saved (left-behind ones dissolve when their chunk unloads; owner); at most OOZING_SLIME_CAP living within 128 blocks of the owner; no loot. | OozingMobEffect, SlimeBlock |
| Silence | Movement game events (step, swim, splash, hit ground, flap, elytra glide) from the wearer are dropped before they reach any listener, each with chance s/cap (all at the cap): sculk sensors, wardens and other mods' hearing all use vanilla game events. | Entity.gameEvent, GameEvent, VibrationSystem |
| Ender | When a projectile would actually hurt the wearer (damage above 0, not an explosion): with chance ENDER_CHANCE_BEST x s/cap, chorus fruit's random teleport instead (diameter from ENDER_DIAMETER by strength) and no damage. | TeleportRandomlyConsumeEffect, EnderMan.hurtServer |
| Breeze | Entity.deflection for the wearer: with chance BREEZE_CHANCE_BEST x s/cap, ProjectileDeflection.REVERSE, as a breeze does. | Breeze.deflection, ProjectileDeflection |
| Infested | The vanilla effect itself (it has one level), for a duration scaled by s. | InfestedMobEffect, Potions.INFESTED |
| Haste | Attribute modifiers: block_break_speed +0.4 x s and attack_speed +0.2 x s (add_multiplied_total). | Player.getDestroySpeed, MobEffects.HASTE, BeaconBlockEntity |
| Absorption | max_absorption +16 x s, filled when the gems are put on (at most once per 30 s, owner), refilled to full 30 s after it was last hit. | AbsorptionMobEffect, Consumables.GOLDEN_APPLE / ENCHANTED_GOLDEN_APPLE |
| Health Boost | Attribute modifier on max_health, +8 x s (exact). | MobEffects.HEALTH_BOOST |
| Dolphin's Grace | On/off made partial: water slow-down moved so the swim-speed gain (1 / (1 - drag)) is s of the potion's: drag = 1 - 1 / (5 + 20 s) from 0.8 (mixin where travelInWater sets 0.96); past 1.0 it swims faster than the potion, never at drag 1. | LivingEntity.travelInWater, DOLPHINS_GRACE_WATER_DRAG, Dolphin |
| Saturation | Restores food and saturation like the vanilla effect (FoodData.eat(n, r) with r = s / cap), at saturation_rate(s) food points per second, whole points as they build up, food only up to saturation_food_target(s). | SaturationMobEffect, FoodData.addExhaustion, Blocks.DANDELION / BLUE_ORCHID |
| Conduit Power | On/off made partial, only while in water or rain: oxygen_bonus s / (1 - s), submerged_mining_speed raised by s of the way to 1.0, underwater fog s of the way to the conduit view. | ConduitBlockEntity, MobEffectUtil.hasWaterBreathing, Attributes.SUBMERGED_MINING_SPEED |
| Hero of the Village | Price hook beside vanilla's (the stronger applies): the hero modifier 0.333 x s, so the best build is 30% cheaper (owner) (mixin at Villager.updateSpecialPrices). Villagers' gifts stay vanilla-only (the effect itself). | Villager.updateSpecialPrices, Raid |
| Wither | Gem Wither mob effect (vanilla's icon; potency in 1% steps); it can kill, as vanilla's does. | WitherSkeleton.doHurtTarget, WitherMobEffect |
| Mining Fatigue | Gem Mining Fatigue mob effect: block_break_speed x 0.027^potency and attack_speed -0.3 x potency. As a drawback: the same, permanent while worn. | ElderGuardian, Player.getDestroySpeed |
| Hunger | Gem Hunger mob effect: causeFoodExhaustion(0.015 x potency) per tick (players only; mobs have no food). As a drawback: the same, permanent while worn. | HungerMobEffect, Consumables.PUFFERFISH / ROTTEN_FLESH |
| Glowing | The vanilla effect itself, for a duration scaled by s. Mostly felt by players (PvP, and gemmed mob gear hitting players). | SpectralArrow |
| Levitation | The vanilla effect itself, for a duration scaled by s. Mostly felt by players (PvP, and gemmed mob gear hitting players). | ShulkerBullet |
| Blindness | The vanilla effect itself, for a duration scaled by s. Mostly felt by players (PvP, and gemmed mob gear hitting players). | Illusioner, Blocks.AZURE_BLUET |
| Nausea | The vanilla effect itself, for a duration scaled by s. Mostly felt by players (PvP, and gemmed mob gear hitting players). | Consumables.PUFFERFISH |
| Darkness | The vanilla effect itself, for a duration scaled by s. Mostly felt by players (PvP, and gemmed mob gear hitting players). | Warden |
| Bad Luck | Attribute modifier on luck, -s. | MobEffects.UNLUCK |

Worn (armor) effects are attribute modifiers, data components or small tick and damage hooks, not potion effect instances: vanilla levels are whole numbers and their icons and timers would claim a full level. Hit-applied (weapon) effects, and weapon drawbacks on the target, are gem mob effects whose amplifier counts strength in 1% steps, with vanilla's icon and timer; a gem arrow carries one as its potion contents with a duration scale of 1. A gem and a potion of the same effect don't add up: the stronger applies (owner).

## Checks (all passed)

- vanilla facts: 132 facts matched against build/mcsrc/26.3
- every ladder step (Infusion level, armor, weapon material, run, grade, potion variant) is at least +4% on the one below; Infusion VI (nether star) and netherite are the only bests; each tier's odds add up to 100%
- a gem's own strength reaches 1.0 only from the strongest potion (lingering) or source item + tier 3 + Infusion VI (nether star), for every craftable gem, so every one can reach the cap (owner); a found-only gem is perfect only from ominous loot at Infusion VI and tier 3
- all 40 status effects in 26.3 are classified: 33 craftable gems, 6 found-only gems, 1 drawback-only, 4 not gems
- 707,281 armor layouts x gem counts enumerated: only full contiguous netherite with 12 gems reaches 0.9; next best 0.874
- 18,821 weapons x gem combinations enumerated: only a netherite weapon with 2 perfect gems reaches 0.9; next best weapon or gem count with perfect gems 0.837
- from the best armor build and the best weapon build, every single step down (potion, base, tier, material, run, one gem fewer, a material-less weapon) loses at least 0.025
- weakest single armor gem (normal potion, Infusion I, tier 1, lone leather piece) = 0.016; early armor kit (iron set, 4 Infusion II tier-1 gems) = 0.087-0.109; weakest weapon gem (wooden sword, Infusion I, tier 1) = 0.058; early weapon (iron sword, 1 Infusion II tier-1 gem) = 0.085-0.106
- stacking: 25,000 random armor and weapon stacks never pass 0.9 x their strongest gem; adding a gem never lowers a total; 12 tier-1 armor gems lose to 4 tier-3 in every set, and 2 tier-1 weapon gems lose to 1 tier-3 on every weapon
- every one of the 39 gems has a worn (armor) and a hit-applied (weapon) form; every worn mapping rises with strength; harmful gems in armor stay short of the vanilla level at the cap; the perfect set reaches the full potion for Strength, Resistance, Turtle Master, Regeneration, Healing, Health Boost, Absorption, Water Breathing, Fire Resistance, Night Vision, Invisibility, Conduit Power, and passes it for Haste 2.5, Jump Boost 2.1921, Dolphin's Grace 1.8, Slow Falling 1.8, Speed 1.875, Luck 1.2 (owner, 2026-11-15)
- healing: best build returns 25% of each non-lethal hit (never a whole hit, so taking damage is always a net loss); early kit 4.9%; every step down from the best loses at least 0.5 points; the curve is flatter than linear
- drawbacks: one is 10% of the strongest vanilla level, any number of one effect stays under 20%, below vanilla's level I for every drawback effect; Poison and Wither roll less often (uncommon weight, owner); Healing, Harming and the rest of the never-drawback list never roll
- inversion: the strongest inverted gem is 0.66 (never perfect); each gem's grade reads back from its strength; roll weights by rarity {'common': 4, 'uncommon': 2, 'rare': 1}
- rolls: each of the 39 gems has one roll table; 'other' pools 11-24 effects, all the main effect's kind and never itself; drawback pools 5-21 effects, all the opposite kind, none on the never-drawback list, and none a direct opposite (13 inverse pairs, the owner's 12 included)
- weapons: per hit, potency rises with strength to the strongest potion's level at the perfect weapon (owner, 2026-11-15); a hit lasts at most 8 s (the best weapon), less below it, never under its floor (owner); a real tipped arrow and a gem of the same effect don't add, the stronger level applies
- loot: 40 vanilla tables get one extra roll (chance 4%-20%); each level's best gem beats the level below; only ominous vaults give perfect gems (any effect, Infusion VI, tier 3), with a drawback except 5% of the time; nowhere else gives a craftable gem Infusion VI; every found-only gem is listed at exactly the levels its source names; every table and item exists in 26.3
